commits.subject: feat(native): search analyzed memory for masked byte patterns (#2341)
commits.body:
feat(native): search analyzed memory for masked byte patterns (#2341)

* feat(native): search analyzed memory for masked byte patterns

The diff adds search_bytes to the CLI, the shared MCP contract, Ghidra
inventory, and the headless bridge, and advertises the same operation on
Hopper as unavailable until that provider is verified. Patterns are
hexadecimal byte pairs with optional ?? wildcards and an optional
equal-length bit mask; the TypeScript boundary and the bridge both
require a nonempty pattern, equal lengths, and at least one constrained
bit. Ghidra walks initialized blocks in address order within inclusive
bounds, keeps overlapping matches inside a single block, and returns
each hit with its segment, unique source file offset, and containing
procedure, continuing through a cursor bound to the target, profile,
pattern, mask, and bounds. Each page reports the inclusive ranges
examined and the skipped uninitialized blocks; cancellation returns a
typed error and discards the active Ghidra database.
address_to_file_offset now uses the same unique-offset helper, which
rejects a mapping that is missing, ambiguous, or larger than a safe
integer.

* fix(native): limit unbounded byte search to loaded memory

Without start or end, search_bytes walked every Ghidra block, including
non-loaded file parts such as .symtab and overlay blocks, which the docs
call out of scope. Unbounded searches now skip those blocks and list them
in searched.skipped_not_loaded; explicit bounds in their address space
still search them. Document that a match must end at or before end.

* fix(native): preserve implicit address spaces in range consumers

* fix(native): reject present malformed byte search state

commits.subject: fix(setup): treat empty DSH_HOME as unset (#2686)
commits.body:
fix(setup): treat empty DSH_HOME as unset (#2686)

* fix(setup): treat empty DSH_HOME as unset (#2666)

The released `@deepseek-ai/dsh-home-paths` package explicitly treats an
empty or whitespace-only `DSH_HOME` as unset and selects the default
Harness home patch. `dshHomeDirectory` previously used nullish coalescing
(`env.DSH_HOME ?? join(home, ".dsh")`), so an empty override flowed
straight through `join(..., "cordis.patch.yml")` and produced a
cwd-relative `cordis.patch.yml` outside the client-selected home.

Treat empty and whitespace-only overrides as unset, matching the sibling
OpenCode override resolver and the released DSH resolver. The patch now
lands at `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` for explicit overrides, the default
`~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml` for empty/unset, and trimmed whitespace for
padded overrides.

Adds `src/application/SupportedClients.test.ts` covering the empty,
whitespace-only, unset, padded, and explicit cases via the public
`supportedClients(...)` entrypoint. Fixes #2666.

* test(setup): remove superseded DSH path unit coverage

ECMA-426 DecodeSourceMapSources reads a content slot only while its index
is within sourcesContent, so a shorter array leaves trailing sources
without content and a longer array adds no sources. Local application
analysis and browser collection rejected any length mismatch and dropped

its separate check because the leaf schema already validates every
supplied entry, and the raw records are still budgeted before parsing.

commits.subject: fix(cli): start on Windows when USERPROFILE is empty (#2345)
commits.body:
fix(cli): start on Windows when USERPROFILE is empty (#2345)

* fix(cli): start on Windows when USERPROFILE is empty

Node's Windows home lookup throws ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR (uv_os_homedir ENOENT)
for an empty USERPROFILE instead of consulting the account profile. Incur
resolves the home while it is imported, so every command, including
`rea --version`, stopped with a raw stack trace before REA ran.

Treat the empty selection as unset in the launcher, before any runtime
import, and cover startup with a compiled-CLI regression.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(process): report no remaining time after a provider deadline fires

Node timers can fire while performance.now() is still a fraction of a
millisecond short of the monotonic deadline. ProviderStartupDeadline then
reported interruption "timeout" and an aborted signal while remainingMs()
returned ceil(0.x) = 1, so polling loops guarded by remainingMs() > 0
(Hopper and Ghidra startup) could run past an elapsed deadline, and the
real-timer test "aborts a bounded wait when its real monotonic deadline
expires" failed intermittently in CI (expected 1 to be 0).

Once the deadline's own timer has classified a timeout, report zero
remaining time. A deterministic regression test fires the timer with the
monotonic clock 0.4 ms short of the deadline.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(browser): attach passive tools to browsers without HTTP discovery (#2346)
commits.body:
feat(browser): attach passive tools to browsers without HTTP discovery (#2346)

* feat(browser): attach passive tools to browsers without HTTP discovery

Accept a literal loopback browser WebSocket,
ws://127.0.0.1:PORT/devtools/browser/ID, as the cdp_endpoint of the six
passive browser tools. Discovery then reads Browser.getVersion and
Target.getTargets over that socket, and the target session adopts the
same socket, so a browser that asks for consent per connection prompts
once per call.

The socket identifier gates access, so Evidence records the endpoint as
ws://127.0.0.1:PORT/devtools/browser/[REDACTED], and runtime
reconciliation accepts that recorded form. HTTP endpoints and their
Evidence are unchanged. Electron, web runtime, scenario and Inspector
endpoints stay HTTP-only.

Refs #2288

* test(browser): match browser-socket captures against HTTP discovery

Check in the real Chrome lane that DevToolsActivePort names the same
browser socket as /json/version, and that inspecting the selected page
through that socket leaves DOM structure and scripts unchanged compared
with an inspection through HTTP discovery.

Refs #2288

* fix(browser): bound browser-socket handshake and report discovery timeouts

Run the browser-socket WebSocket handshake and both discovery commands
under one discovery deadline, so a port that accepts the connection but
never completes the upgrade times out instead of waiting forever.

Report a reached deadline as a timeout without carrying the internal
abort as its cause, so CLI and MCP project provider_timeout rather than
cancelled. Caller cancellation is still reported as cancelled.

Refs #2288

commits.subject: fix(native): parse renamed dyld_info re-exports (#2364)
commits.body:
fix(native): parse renamed dyld_info re-exports (#2364)

* fix(native): parse renamed dyld_info re-exports

dyld_info prints a re-export whose name differs from the source library's
symbol as `[re-export] _foo_renamed (_foo from libfoo)`. The export parser
only accepted `(from libfoo)`, so inspect_macho reported a nonexistent
export named `_foo_renamed (_foo from libfoo)` with no source, and the nm
row for `_foo_renamed` survived the name-based merge as a second export
with reexport null.

Accept the optional source symbol, trying the plain `(from lib)` form
first so a library name containing ` from ` keeps its text. The row now
reports `_foo_renamed` re-exported from libfoo and replaces the nm
duplicate. The export schema has no field for the source symbol name, so
exports coverage records a limitation when a renamed re-export is present.
The golden fixture is a dyld_info capture of a synthetic dylib linked with
-Wl,-alias,_foo,_foo_renamed.

* fix(native): split dyld re-export suffix without nested quantifiers

Replace the (?:(.+?)\s+)??from lazy-optional group with a linear string
scan so malformed lines cannot backtrack and a library path containing
" from " still keeps its whole text via the plain-form-first check.

* test(native): cover nested re-export library names

* fix(native): retain reexports missing from nm inventory

commits.subject: fix(javascript-semantics): keep emitted data out of dispatch listener fields (#2952)
commits.body:
fix(javascript-semantics): keep emitted data out of dispatch listener fields (#2952)

* fix(javascript-semantics): keep emitted data out of dispatch listener fields

The EventEmitter operation collector read argument position 1 as the
listener for every event method, so a dispatch such as
bus.emit("ready", data) reported the data binding and its range as the
listener. Only registration and removal name a listener there; emit
passes its remaining arguments to listeners that already exist. Read the
listener argument only for register and remove operations.

Fixes #2574

* fix(javascript-semantics): read listener arguments only for listener-taking methods

removeAllListeners accepts only an optional event name, so gating the
listener argument on operation kind still reported an ignored second
argument as a listener. Gate on the methods whose argument position 1
names a listener instead: the registration methods, off, and
removeListener.

commits.body:
perf(javascript): defer ambiguity expansion in version comparisons (#2962)

perf(javascript): avoid quadratic temporary matching state

Repeated source groups can allocate candidates that later identity matches
discard. Retain the original ambiguous groups until all tiers finish, expand
only unmatched survivors, and append to locally owned key buckets in place.

Constraint: Preserve matching priority, full ambiguity, and public output.
Directive: Do not re-match residual groups that become unique after later tiers.

Tested: CLI benchmarks and full-suite failure comparison on the recorded base.
Not-tested: Full suite on the updated main; native Linux and Windows workflows.

fix(wasm): report WABT output past its budget as a resource constraint (#2117)

* fix(wasm): report WABT output past its budget as a resource constraint

A module whose WAT exceeds the 32 MiB output budget failed as
unreadable_output, advised `rea doctor`, and echoed the full 32 MiB
truncated WAT prefix in details.captured_output. Map the owned-command
output-limit outcome during inspection to AnalysisResourceConstraintError
naming the budget, as the apktool and native macOS providers do, with a
remediation that says the fixed budget will not change on retry.

Captured output for an output-limit failure keeps only the first 4,096
characters of each stream, including on the cleanup-failure path. An
oversized --version probe keeps its configuration-phase mapping.

* fix(wasm): keep observed sizes and whole code points in output-limit excerpts

Cut each stream's output-limit excerpt with boundedUtf8Text at 4,096
UTF-8 bytes, so an astral character at the cut no longer leaves a lone
surrogate. Mark the output truncated when either excerpt was cut, and
report each stream's observed byte count.

Word the remediation as a fact about the fixed budget. A flood of
diagnostics from any WABT tool reaches this path, so it no longer says
the module is too large.

Replace the 32 MiB end-to-end test with a launcher seam that raises a
small output-limit failure.

* fix(wasm): match sibling captured-output fields for WABT output limits

Report retained byte counts in stdout_bytes and stderr_bytes, as apktool
and the firmware command do, and record exit_code and signal. Mark the
excerpt truncated outright, since the command raises output-limit only
after retention was truncated.

When cleanup also fails, record the output limit and its budget as the
previous error instead of the generic command message. Document that
the two streams share the budget, so the excerpt holds up to 4,096 of
the bytes each stream retained.

* docs(wasm): scope the output-budget error to inspection commands

* docs(wasm): distinguish reported warm costs from unmeasured gaps

* docs(wasm): clarify the scope of reported warm measurements

commits.subject: feat(managed): decode ldstr user strings in member inspection (#2162)
commits.body:
feat(managed): decode ldstr user strings in member inspection (#2162)

* feat(managed): decode ldstr user strings in member inspection

inspect_managed_members reported every ldstr operand as a bare 0x70 token,
so an analyst could see that a method loads a literal but not which one.
Answering "where is this path or key used" required a second tool.

Read the optional #US stream and add a top-level user_strings inventory:
each distinct token loaded by an inspected method body, once, in token
order, with its #US file offset and decoded UTF-16 value. Instruction
anchors and normalized CIL digests keep their build-local tokens. A missing
#US stream or malformed item is reported against its token as partial
coverage. Evidence recorded before this field reads user_strings as null.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): collect user strings only from ldstr

A malformed ldtoken can carry a 0x70 token, which the operand decoder
classifies as a string operand. Only ldstr loads a literal, so collect
user strings by opcode.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): admit user-string tokens and failures before collecting them

Charge each distinct ldstr token to the decode budget before adding it to
the collection set, and admit each #US failure before retaining it. A
missing #US stream is now one stream-level issue rather than one per
token.

Document why the #US terminal flag is not validated: Mono and Roslyn
assemblies disagree with ECMA-335 II.24.2.4 and the runtime ignores it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(managed): describe missing #US reporting and the unvalidated flag byte

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(managed): cover #US items that run past the stream end

An odd length whose payload crosses the end of #US, and a two-byte
length prefix that starts on the last #US byte, are both rejected as
"User string leaves #US" beside a readable literal. The test fails if
that bounds check is removed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): report reserved #US length prefixes as string failures

The compressed-length reader shared by #Blob and #US hard-coded
invalid-blob and "Metadata blob" for a reserved prefix, so a malformed
user string was published as a blob failure. The caller now names the
item it reads: #Blob keeps its code and message, and #US reports
invalid-string.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): append member inspection issues without argument spreading

inspectManagedMembersBytes gathered every producer's issues with
issues.push(...list), passing one argument per issue. A large malformed
input, such as hundreds of thousands of distinct bad ldstr operands or
MemberRef rows, overflows the stack with an untyped RangeError instead of
returning partial coverage. All six sites now use
appendManagedParseIssues, which appends one issue at a time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): classify truncated #US and #Blob length prefixes by item

A two- or four-byte compressed-length prefix cut off by the end of the
artifact went through the generic range check and was reported as
invalid-row. The prefix reader now uses the item's own code for both
reserved and truncated prefixes: invalid-string for #US, invalid-blob for
#Blob. The unused generic range helper is removed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): retain user-string terminal flag conformance issues

* test(managed): write ECMA-335 #US terminal flags and cover flag issues

d5b7b0704 reports a #US terminal flag that differs from ECMA-335
II.24.2.4. The fixture heap always wrote 0, so its non-Latin-1 literals
now read as nonconforming. The fixture writes the spec flag, and a new
test flips one flag each way ("ok" set to 1, "it's" set to 0) and checks
that both literals remain beside one issue each.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): classify ldstr operands before collapsing a missing #US

With no #US stream, every collected ldstr operand was counted as a #US
reference and reported only as missing-stream, while the same non-0x70
operand got invalid-heap-index when the stream existed. parseUserStrings
now owns which operands are user-string tokens: any other operand is
invalid-heap-index either way, and only 0x70 tokens count toward the
missing-stream issue. The heap reader drops its duplicate kind check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): state user-string limits in member comparisons

compare_managed_members ignored user_strings, so a method whose ldstr
literal changed at the same token, or legacy Evidence that never examined
literals, could read as unchanged with no caveat. The comparison now adds
an unknown limitation when either side predates user strings and a
not-compared limitation when literals were observed. ExportedType and
user-string inventories share one uncomparedInventory rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(managed): advertise ldstr literals in member inspection help

The MCP tool description, the type_names input, and the CLI command and
--type help now say that inspect_managed_members returns the #US string
literals that ldstr loads, and that a type selection limits them to the
literals the selected types' method bodies load.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): read the empty #US entry at offset 0

ECMA-335 II.24.2.4 makes the first #US entry the empty blob: a zero
length with no terminal flag byte. ldstr 0x70000000 loads it, but the
odd-length check rejected it as invalid-string, dropping the literal and
making coverage partial. Offset 0 with length 0 now reads as "".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): reserve #US offset 0 and admit literals before scanning

Offset 0 is the reserved empty #US entry, so a nonempty item there is now
invalid-string instead of a published literal. The literal's projection
is reserved before the terminal-flag scan, so an inadmissible item fails
at the budget without reading every code unit. The scan's loop index no
longer shadows the token's heap index.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): report #US length prefixes wider than ECMA-335 assigns

compressedLength accepted an overlong encoding, such as 0x80 0x05 for a
5-byte item, without comment. It now reports whether the width is the
one ECMA-335 II.23.2 assigns, and the #US reader reports a non-minimal
prefix as an invalid-string conformance issue beside the readable
literal, like the terminal flag. readMetadataUserString returns every
issue it observes. #Blob behavior is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): check the #US length width before the empty entry

The offset-0 empty entry returned "" before the length-width check, so an
overlong empty entry such as 0x80 0x00 read as complete. The width issue
is now collected first and returned with the empty literal.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): admit #US width issues only for returned literals

The overlong-prefix issue was reserved before the fatal shape checks, so
an item that then failed, such as 0x80 0x00 away from offset 0, leaked
512 bytes of budget per token. The width issue is now built and admitted
only on paths that return the literal.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): keep #US issues out of member metadata status

User-string issues, including terminal-flag and length-prefix
conformance differences, marked metadata.status partial, so
compare_managed_members turned one-sided methods and fields into unknown
even though every member row was examined. #US issues now make coverage
partial while metadata.status describes the member inventory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): give user strings their own coverage

#US issues entered the member coverage, so every consumer that reads it
as member coverage (application graph member facts, comparison status)
reported examined members as partial over a literal conformance
difference. user_strings is now { state, literals, issues }: #US issues
live there and never change the member coverage or metadata.status.
parseUserStrings returns that inventory directly.

compare_managed_members inspects with user strings skipped, since it
never reads literals, so a large literal cannot exhaust the decode budget
of a comparison. Its limitations state once that literals are not
compared, and the ExportedType limitations return to their main form.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): mark user strings partial when a body is not fully decoded

With user strings owning their coverage, an inspected method body that
was partial, malformed, or truncated no longer reached their state, so a
literal after the decode stopped was missing from a "complete" inventory.
parseUserStrings now marks the inventory partial unless every inspected
body was fully decoded, keeping the literals it did observe.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): mark user strings partial when a method row is omitted

A MethodDef row that failed before its body was read was recorded as an
issue and omitted, so its ldstr instructions were never scanned, yet the
user-string inventory could still read as complete. parseUserStrings now
takes the parseMethods result and stays partial whenever a method row
failed, as well as when an inspected body was not fully decoded.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): count only method rows that may hide a selected body

Any parseMethods issue marked user strings partial, including an
unreadable name on a method outside the type selection, so a fully
scanned selection read as incomplete. parseMethods now reads each row's
owner first and reports unscannedRows: rows that produced no method while
their owner is selected or unknown. parseUserStrings uses that count.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): treat unreadably named types as possibly selected

Under a type_names selection, a type whose name could not be read may be
a requested type, but its methods were skipped without counting toward
unscannedRows, so an unexamined body left user strings complete. A
method whose owner's name is unreadable now counts as possibly selected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): judge user-string scans by CIL decoding, not body status

body.status is malformed for an invalid exception section even when
every instruction decoded, so user strings read as partial although every
ldstr was examined. The body reader now reports whether its CIL was fully
scanned, independent of exception-region validity, and parseMethods folds
unscanned bodies and unproduced rows into one unscannedMethods count that
parseUserStrings uses instead of reinterpreting body.status.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): stop deduplicating user-string issues

The inventory passed its issues through uniqueManagedParseIssues, which
serializes every issue into an unbudgeted map: about 42 MB of heap and
113 ms for 125,000 issues on Node 24. The issues are unique by
construction (one failure or per-offset conformance issues per distinct
token, one missing-stream issue), so the inventory now returns them, and
its literals, without copies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(managed): preserve selected string coverage unknowns

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: morluto <76467478+morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.subject: perf(javascript): reuse semantic member-mutation lookups (#2941)
commits.body:
perf(javascript): reuse semantic member-mutation lookups (#2941)

The semantic member-mutation collector revisits the same nodes while it closes
alias chains, and each visit re-derived results that cannot change within the
phase:

- resolveSemanticBindingState re-walked the scope chain for the same identifier
  node. Definition collection completes before this phase, and addBinding is
  reachable only from it, so a scope's bindings no longer change.
- directInitializerPosition, directMutationPosition and
  referenceInitializerPosition are pure functions of a node and the analysis
  parent map, but were recomputed for every mutation and initializer.
- markValue re-encoded the same capture tuple with JSON.stringify and built a
  fresh long key for every Set/Map lookup, so each lookup re-hashed the whole
  key. The capture key is now cached per binding, origin and owner, and the
  lifetime key is derived from it.

On pdfjs-dist 5.3.93 wasm/openjpeg_nowasm_fallback.js (462316 bytes, sha256
53c228428a8861035a34738966af263fc9d4cee6df25a0ad942af947469a0bd9) the semantic
phase takes 177.8 s instead of 272.9 s in-process, with a byte-identical
semantic IR. With --max-heap-mb 3072 and the default heap the base revision
exhausts the worker; with the default 300 s per-source deadline raised, the
completed CLI run takes 240.6 s instead of 396.7 s and its output is identical
apart from volatile identifiers.

Refs #2498

commits.subject: fix(verify-package): read Hopper installer applicability from its owner (#2973)
commits.body:
fix(verify-package): read Hopper installer applicability from its owner (#2973)

* fix(verify-package): read Hopper installer applicability from its owner

packageSetupSupport derived hopperSetupSupported from the general doctor
host check plus a non-Windows condition, so a Debian-family host REA
supports but the Hopper package never tested reported an automated
installer the packaged setup never offers. verifySetupApply then expected
needs_confirmation for the explicit --install-hopper request and failed
at verify-package-setup.mjs:403.

Applicability now comes from readLinuxDistribution() in the built
application, so the verifier follows the predicate the package ships, and
it stays unknown when no distribution can be read instead of collapsing
into a known-unsupported host. Generic agent configuration and idempotence
assertions stay independent of installer applicability, and the expected
status is still derived from the host rather than from the request being
asserted.

Verified on Kali 2026.3, a Debian-family host with an installer-untested
distribution and the simulated Hopper package environment: before the
change npm run verify:package fails at verify-package-setup.mjs:403 with
the packaged setup correctly returning needs_human; after it the same run
passes every stage. Both applicability branches are covered by
tests/evaluation/package/packageSetupSupport.test.ts, which runs in the
source lane without a build. No real Hopper installation was exercised,
so no engine compatibility claim follows.

Refs #2939

commits.subject: test(process): preserve terminal deadline expiry regression (#2055)
commits.body:
test(process): preserve terminal deadline expiry regression (#2055)

* fix(cli): preserve import-map option descriptions

* fix(process): report no remaining time after a provider deadline fires

Node timers can fire while performance.now() is still a fraction of a
millisecond short of the monotonic deadline. ProviderStartupDeadline then
reported interruption "timeout" and an aborted signal while remainingMs()
returned ceil(0.x) = 1, so polling loops guarded by remainingMs() > 0
(Hopper and Ghidra startup) could run past an elapsed deadline, and the
real-timer test "aborts a bounded wait when its real monotonic deadline
expires" failed intermittently in CI (expected 1 to be 0).

Once the deadline's own timer has classified a timeout, report zero
remaining time. A deterministic regression test fires the timer with the
monotonic clock 0.4 ms short of the deadline.

comments, or only a `---` marker, also parses to a null YAML document.
Setup still rejected it as malformed ("expected record, received null")
and reported Hermes as invalid.

Treat a null Hermes document as holding no settings, as #1983 does for
an empty file. The serializer already edits a comment-only document in

replace it with a map and keep the comments written after the marker.

no source text, holds no settings. An explicit null or ~ is a value, so
setup and uninstall reject it as before, the same as any other non-map
root.

the multiple-document rejection into their own block.

parseDocument with options returns a Document.Parsed, whose contents

commits.body:
feat(ghidra): admit 32-bit big-endian PowerPC ELF (#1747)

* feat(ghidra): admit 32-bit big-endian PowerPC ELF

Recognize EM_PPC as a provider-neutral `powerpc` family that keeps its ELF
class, byte order, type and flags, and admit ELF32 big-endian ET_EXEC through
a bounded Ghidra lane. ELF64, little-endian, relocatable/shared objects and
EF_PPC_EMB are refused with a specific reason; Hopper and IDA do not gain
PowerPC support, and Windows Ghidra P0 is unchanged.

Ghidra's ELF loader selects PowerPC:BE:32:e500:default for a plain EM_PPC
header, which misreads 750-family code. The lane binds
PowerPC:BE:32:default/default in the profile (language_selection
"admitted-lane-v1"), imports with it and checks the reported language. A
language set through REA_GHIDRA_LANGUAGE_ID still replaces the lane default.

Add a source-owned fixture, fixed-encoding probe, GNU readelf cross-check and
the optional `verify:ghidra:ppc` real-provider lane, plus docs/ghidra-ppc.md.

commits.subject: fix(managed): pair members by declared identity before name-free remaps (#2116)
commits.body:
fix(managed): pair members by declared identity before name-free remaps (#2116)

* fix(managed): pair members by declared identity before name-free remaps

The first matching round keyed methods on signature and normalized CIL,
and fields on signature, without the declared type or name. Identical
members of different types fell into one ambiguous group, so a file
compared with itself reported unknowns, and a lone match across types
was reported as an unchanged exact pair while the member's own
counterpart went unpaired.

Pair by declared type, name, and exact CIL/signature first, then by
declared type, name, and raw signature. The name-free CIL/signature,
field-signature, and structural rounds now run last, as remaps, and
skip a pair across declared identities while either member's own type
and name remain unpaired on the other side.

Nested types that share a bare name still share one declared identity,
so their identical members stay ambiguous in a self-comparison.

* fix(managed): keep members with kept identities out of remap rounds

The cross-identity check applied only to one-to-one groups. A member
whose own declared type and name were still unpaired on the other side
could fall into a larger remap group and be reported ambiguous, and a
blocked candidate could make an otherwise unique remap ambiguous.

A remap round now drops such members before grouping, along with
members whose declaring type is unresolved. Same-identity structural
pairs get their own round before the remaps. Each member's declared
identity is computed once.

Ambiguity limitations now name the evidence a group shares, which
stays true whether the round keyed on names or not.

* fix(managed): keep names in unresolved identities and hold ambiguous ones

A member of an unresolved declaring type had no declared identity, so
the declared-identity rounds keyed it by CIL or signature alone. Two
unresolved members with different names paired as an exact match, and
a file compared with itself reported unresolved members ambiguous.

The declared identity now always includes the name, with a null type
for an unresolved one. Remap rounds still leave such members out.

A remap round now also leaves out a member whose own identity sits in
an ambiguous group on the other side, not only one left one-sided.

The undecoded-counterpart check uses the same declared identity.

* fix(managed): keep remap groups with unresolved owners ambiguous

Remap rounds dropped members of an unresolved declaring type before
grouping. Such a member can be another member's own counterpart, so a
resolved member could remap to a copy in another type while its
unresolved counterpart was reported added.

Unresolved members now join remap grouping, and a group that contains
one stays ambiguous instead of pairing.

The undecoded-counterpart set reuses each member's computed identity.

* fix(managed): keep ownerless members out of declared rounds when shared

A member whose declaring type did not resolve has a declared identity
of a null type and its name. The declared rounds paired two such
same-named members even when the other side also held a resolved
member with the same CIL and signature, which could be the owner. The
old name-free first round reported that group as ambiguous.

An ownerless member now enters the declared rounds only when no other
member on either side shares its exact CIL/signature key, and never
the declared structural round. Otherwise it reaches the remap rounds,
which keep any group with an unresolved member ambiguous.

* fix(managed): keep competitors of an ownerless member out of the declared round

When an ownerless member shares its exact CIL/signature key with another
member on the same side, its owner may be that member. The resolved
members holding the key now stay out of the declared round too, so they
cannot pair and consume the candidate the ownerless member may own, and
the remap round keeps the whole group ambiguous as main does. A lone
ownerless member still pairs with its lone counterpart.

* test(managed): split the ownerless comparison tests under the function length limit

The ownerless describe block reached 181 lines, past oxlint's
max-lines-per-function limit of 150. Move the structural-competitor
case into its own block.

* fix(managed): contest signatures and remap only open candidates

* fix(managed): retain blocked raw-signature choices as unknown

* fix(managed): keep member names in signature contention

* fix(managed): scope residual signature contention by name once

ownerlessContested applies competitionIdentityKey itself, but
unresolvedSignatureAmbiguities passed it keys that were already
name-scoped, so the contested set never matched the groups and the
same-signature, different-body case reported additions and removals
instead of one unknown group. Pass the raw signature key.

* fix(managed): constrain matchObserved to declared members

matchObserved passes its items to matchByKeys, which needs Declared, so
its looser { declaring_type } bound failed typecheck (TS2344, TS2322).

* fix(managed): retain held ownership contention for residual matches

* fix(test): bind workspace fixture in Hopper launch cases

* fix(ci): prepare worker tests and preserve Hopper cleanup ordering

commits.subject: fix(cli): refuse a JavaScript integrity policy the binary analyze lane cannot honor (#2808)
commits.body:
fix(cli): refuse a JavaScript integrity policy the binary analyze lane cannot honor (#2808)

* fix(cli): refuse an integrity policy the binary analyze lane cannot honor

`analyze` declares --integrity-policy for its JavaScript lane and forwards it
only there. On a binary target the flag was accepted and then dropped:
inspect_artifact-style integrity handling does not exist on this path, and
binary_overview is a strictObject with no input at all, so the request could
never take effect and the run proceeded as if the caller had not asked.

The same branch already refuses source_paths on a binary target with a typed
AnalysisInputError, and the sibling `inspect` command refuses the flag outright,
so the refusal is the established handling here. The policy option carries a
default, so the check keys off a value that differs from the owner schema's own
default rather than the flag's presence; otherwise every binary analyze would be
refused. The default is read from the schema instead of being restated.

Verified with 5 integrity policy CLI cases, check:fast and
verify:test-discovery (1023 files) on macOS arm64, and by running the built CLI
for the no-flag, explicit-default and record-and-continue cases. The regression
case failed with the command reaching the binary lane before the change.

* fix(cli): reject explicit default integrity policies for binaries

* fix(cli): keep an omitted integrity policy absent on the binary lane

`javascriptApplicationOptions.shape.integrityPolicy` fills an omission with its
default, and `.optional()` keeps reporting that parsed value, so
`options.integrityPolicy !== undefined` was true for every `analyze <target>`
call: ordinary binary analysis was rejected before the target was even read.

List `z.undefined()` first in a union so an omitted option stays absent while
the owner still validates a supplied value, and reapply the owner's metadata so
help and `--schema` keep describing the option.

Validation: tests/boundary/cli/javascriptIntegrityPolicyCli.test.ts reports
1 failed | 5 passed without this change (the case "still routes a binary
analyze target without an integrity policy" returned invalid_request for
integrity_policy instead of reaching the target) and 6 passed with it;
`npm run check:fast` passes on macOS 26.5.1 arm64 with Node.js 24.18.0.

* fix(cli): omit integrity defaults from binary option schema

* test(ci): isolate report fixtures and declare PowerPC Java bounds

commits.subject: fix(electron): reject non-executable paths and contain launch rejections (#2705)
commits.body:
fix(electron): reject non-executable paths and contain launch rejections (#2705)

* fix(electron): reject non-executable paths and contain launch rejections

An executable_path that runs but never prints the inspector line made
Playwright's electron.launch() leave three waits unawaited. They rejected
unhandled and Node ended the CLI or the MCP server (#2269).

Check the resolved executable_path is a regular file, and on non-Windows
hosts that it passes X_OK, before any launch. Wrap only the launch call
in a scoped unhandledRejection listener that absorbs rejections whose
stack is in playwright-core/lib and re-throws anything else.

Tested on Linux with Node 22.23.1, 24.18.0 and 26.11.1.

Refs #2269

🤖 Generated with Claude Code (Sonnet 5.5, verified by Opus 5.5) 🦊

* fix(electron): absorb only this launch's orphaned rejections

The listener around the launch dropped every rejection with a
playwright-core stack, so an unrelated Playwright failure during the
launch window would vanish. Hold those rejections instead. When the
launch settles, drop only the ones whose message is part of the launch's
own error (the orphans of a failed launch). Raise every other one again
through the unhandledRejection path, so the process still fails. A launch
that succeeds raises all of them. Rejections without a Playwright stack
still fail at once.

One setImmediate turn before the decision lets rejections queued by the
settling tick arrive first. It is a single turn, not a timer. A shared
set of absorbed errors stops overlapping launches from raising each
other's orphans. The listener is removed on every path.

Add child-process tests that drive the built provider through its launch
seam, since Vitest's worker has its own unhandledRejection listener.

commits.subject: fix(reference): report entries beyond the path limit as I/O failures (#2716)
commits.body:
fix(reference): report entries beyond the path limit as I/O failures (#2716)

* fix(reference): report entries beyond the path limit as I/O failures

Reference-source traversal joins each child onto the root path. A valid
tree whose nested entries exceed the platform's absolute path limit
(PATH_MAX 1024 on macOS) makes lstat fail with ENAMETOOLONG. The
reader's filesystem error allow-list lacked that code, so
filesystemFailureDetail returned undefined and the native rejection
escaped both readReferenceSource and importReferenceSource instead of
becoming the existing failed `io` entry.

Add ENAMETOOLONG to the allow-list, matching the JavaScript application
reader's list. Readable siblings stay in the graph and the unreachable
entry is recorded with its OS message.

Fixes #2652

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(reference): assert the imported graph keeps readable and failed entries

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(process): report no remaining time after a provider deadline fires

Node timers can fire while performance.now() is still a fraction of a
millisecond short of the monotonic deadline. ProviderStartupDeadline then
reported interruption "timeout" and an aborted signal while remainingMs()
returned ceil(0.x) = 1, so polling loops guarded by remainingMs() > 0
(Hopper and Ghidra startup) could run past an elapsed deadline, and the
real-timer test "aborts a bounded wait when its real monotonic deadline
expires" failed intermittently in CI (expected 1 to be 0).

Once the deadline's own timer has classified a timeout, report zero
remaining time. A deterministic regression test fires the timer with the
monotonic clock 0.4 ms short of the deadline.

Directory-only secret and ignore rules now also match an unknown-kind
entry (it may be a directory), and the summary counts unknown entries

commits.subject: fix(capture): end special-scheme URL authorities at a backslash (#2767)
commits.body:
fix(capture): end special-scheme URL authorities at a backslash (#2767)

* fix(capture): end special-scheme URL authorities at a backslash

The native mitmproxy adapter removed transport userinfo with
`^(...//)[^/?#]*@`, so the authority ran to the last "@" before "/", "?"
or "#". For `https://example.test\part@tail` it treated
`example.test\part` as userinfo, reported `https://tail` as the
Location, and withdrew the original bytes as a transport credential.
WHATWG URL parsing, used by the shared TypeScript owner
(recordedTransportUrl.ts) and by HAR captures, ends a special-scheme or
scheme-relative authority at a backslash, so that "@" is ordinary path
text.

Locate the authority with the same boundary rule before removing
userinfo. Bytes are handled as Latin-1 text so unrelated bytes stay
identical. Userinfo before the backslash is still removed and redacted.
Add source unit tests for the adapter projection to test:python.

Fixes #2671

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(capture): skip special-scheme leading slashes before userinfo

Ending the authority at a backslash exposed a credential: for
`https://\user:pass@host/path`, WHATWG parsing skips every leading "/"
or "\" after a special scheme (and in scheme-relative references), so
`user:pass` is userinfo, but the new boundary stopped at the first
backslash and found no "@". The same applied to `https:\\user:pass@host`
and `https:user:pass@host`.

Start the authority after that whole slash run for non-file special
schemes and scheme-relative references. File URLs keep their "//"
boundary because they carry no userinfo. Load the adapter in tests with
fresh mitmproxy stand-ins scoped to its import instead of leaving them
in sys.modules.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(capture): parse URL controls and mixed network authorities

* fix(capture): distinguish native paths and URL base authorities

* fix(capture): preserve file-relative path evidence after separators

* fix(comparison): recheck historical calls-only changes (#2223)

* fix(comparison): preserve incomplete function call evidence

Keep missing, unknown, partial and unresolved call relationships unknown in function comparisons and reconstruction claims. Aggregate IDA caller and callee coverage without overwriting uncertainty.

Validate with 144 focused tests, typecheck/lint, docs checks and test discovery. Real providers were not verified; the full headless IDA session suite requires unavailable Windows native controls.

* fix(comparison): recheck historical calls-only changes

---------

Co-authored-by: morluto <76467478+morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(android): make DEX descriptor pattern portable

* fix(ci): isolate Linux Hopper process fixture inventory

* fix(capture): remove empty URL userinfo markers

* test(capture): cover empty URL userinfo markers

* test(ci): isolate Hopper process inventory fixtures

* fix(ci): declare process inventory callback

* test(ci): isolate alternate launcher process fixture

* fix(capture): keep URLs that WHATWG rejects instead of redacting userinfo

File URLs cannot carry userinfo (an "@" in a file host fails the parse),
and a special authority whose host or port WHATWG rejects fails the whole
URL. Neither has credentials, so the bridge now keeps their source text
and byte sidecar. Checked against Node's URL over 30,000 spellings: no
under-redaction, over-redaction 20,540 -> 5,865 (remaining: empty
userinfo, IPv4 range, IDNA, non-special and baseless references).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(capture): strip trailing URL whitespace and validate IP hosts and ports

The previous host check counted trailing C0 controls and spaces, which
WHATWG strips, so `https://user:pw@host ` kept its password. Trailing
C0/space is now removed from the parse view (raw offsets are unchanged).

Special hosts now also follow the WHATWG IPv4 parser (ends-in-a-number,
hex/octal parts, range) and IPv6 literal syntax (zone IDs rejected), and
ports are bounded lexically before int(), which raised ValueError past
4300 digits on Python 3.11+ and failed the whole capture.

Node URL differential over 126,000 spellings: under-redaction 8,084 -> 0,
ValueError 2,550 -> 0; remaining special-scheme over-redaction is IDNA
and the pinned empty-userinfo case. Cost: +0.6 us per URL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(capture): redact userinfo before hosts that need Unicode mapping

A non-ASCII special host may map under UTS #46 to an accepted host
(fullwidth digits, ideographic full stops, ignored code points), so
treat it as accepted instead of running the ASCII IPv4 check on it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(native): derive Mach-O word size and byte order from the selected slice (#3163)
commits.body:
fix(native): derive Mach-O word size and byte order from the selected slice (#3163)

* fix(native): derive Mach-O word size and byte order from the selected slice

inspect_macho read endian and word_size from `file -b` for the whole
file. macOS `file` never prints a Mach-O byte order, so endian was null
for every target. For a universal binary, word_size matched "64-bit"
anywhere in the summary instead of describing the selected slice, and it
was null for a thin 32-bit slice.

Both now come from the selected slice's otool header: the magic gives
the word size and the CPU family gives the byte order (x86 and ARM
little, PowerPC big, other families unknown). The file capture is no
longer needed by inspect_macho, so it is no longer run there.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(native): skip llvm-nm's dyld-info pass when the symbol table names every export (#3200)

* perf(native): skip llvm-nm's dyld-info pass when the symbol table names every export

inspect_macho ran `nm -gjU`, whose default dyld-info pass takes seconds on
large apps (Keynote arm64 5.8 s, x86_64 10.2 s) yet under -gU can only add
export-trie names that dyld_info -exports already reports. Run
`nm -gjU --no-dyldinfo` and rerun the default pass only when dyld_info
reports an export the symbol table lacks (e.g. strip -T), so its exact
names still disambiguate dyld_info rows.

commits.subject: fix(sqlite): keep a retained worker owner after a failed worker exit (#3242)
commits.body:
fix(sqlite): keep a retained worker owner after a failed worker exit (#3242)

* fix: abort invalid JSON parses and keep retained worker owners

Main (7375ab6e3) fails four boundary tests from its latest batch.

- f79fd59e9 moved JSON value validation into a non-aborting superRefine, so
  authenticated Evidence still computed its recursive identity digest over
  a 10,000-level `parameters` value and overflowed the stack. The process
  comparison CLI then reported "Maximum call stack size exceeded" instead of
  the depth limit. Abort the parse on a JSON validation issue so enclosing
  refinements never walk invalid data.
- runOwnedCommand retains an incomplete cleanup through retainCleanup and
  then rethrows the command failure without a cleanupOwner. The EVM and SQLite
  providers replaced their retained owner with that undefined value, so an
  output-limit failure with unresolved cleanup lost cleanupIncomplete and its
  owner. Keep the retained owner unless the failure carries one.
- The EVM malformed-reply test expected a nonexistent `output_failure` code;
  AnalysisOutputError projects to `unreadable_output`. The pcap capinfos stub
  prints its report with a trailing newline, which retained output preserves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(sqlite): keep a retained worker owner after a failed worker exit

Cover the path the existing worker-cleanup test bypasses: a real owned worker
exits nonzero, runOwnedCommand retains its incomplete cleanup and rethrows the
failure without a cleanupOwner. The provider must still report
cleanupIncomplete and block a new worker until the retained cleanup succeeds.
Fails on the previous owner assignment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(evm): retain the compact worker failure beside retained cleanup

When the worker command fails and its cleanup is retained, the cleanup error
now reports the primary failure in the same compact form as an unretained
command cleanup failure: failure kind, message, exit code and signal. Its
output is already retained once as captured_output, so the previous error no
longer repeats up to a megabyte of diagnostics, and failure_kind stays at the
top level that the provider test reads. Both paths share
ownedCommandPreviousError.

commits.subject: fix(artifacts): inventory universal slices REA cannot structurally index (#3283)
commits.body:
fix(artifacts): inventory universal slices REA cannot structurally index (#3283)

* fix(artifacts): inventory universal slices REA cannot structurally index

inspect_artifact and extract_artifact rejected a valid universal Mach-O
when one slice was outside the structural index, such as XLD's
big-endian PowerPC slice. The whole inventory failed with "Artifact is
invalid or has changed. Get a fresh copy and try again."

When lipo reports every slice's range, the slices are now inventoried
from those ranges with a limitation naming the unsupported structure,
as the reader already does for files without structural facts. When
lipo omits a range, the failure is reported as unavailable support
rather than a corrupt artifact.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(artifacts): validate every FAT slice past an unsupported one

readFatSlices returned at the first unsupported slice, so a later
malformed slice went unchecked: with lipo's ranges now inventoried for
unsupported structure, a malformed little-endian slice after a
big-endian one was accepted while the reverse order was rejected.
Unsupported slices are now remembered and the remaining slices are
still validated, so malformed structure wins in either order.

Adds portable fake-lipo coverage for complete ranges, missing ranges
(unavailable) and malformed slices on both sides of a big-endian slice.
